statements.venue: Written statement to the Bangor Daily News
statements.quote: The best path forward will balance a recognition of AI’s promise — including breakthroughs in medical advances and accessibility — with its risks
statements.context: Collins was responding to an article on how Maine politicians were reacting to warnings from AI researchers, including a departing Anthropic researcher who said the technology could kill everyone.
statements.reason: She mentions AI's "risks" only generically and the remedies she names are consumer protections and critical infrastructure, so catastrophic risk is not acknowledged, although the remark was made in reply to extinction warnings.

slowdown.note: No statement for or against slowing frontier AI development was found.

pause.note: No statement for or against a pause on frontier AI development was found. Her 2025 vote was against a moratorium on state AI regulation, which is a different thing.

intl.note: No statement on coordinating with China on the pace of AI was found, and she did not sign the 23 September 2026 letter urging such talks; the Bangor Daily News says she backs keeping the US ahead of China on AI, which does not count.
sources: Letter from 17 senators to President Trump, 23 September 2026

rsi.note: No statement on a ban on self-improving AI was found.

record: Voted in 2025 with nearly the whole Senate to remove a proposed 10-year moratorium on state AI regulation from the budget bill.
Did not sign the 23 September 2026 letter from 17 senators urging President Trump to pursue an AI agreement with China; her name is not among the 17 signatures.
Letter text (Senate Commerce Committee copy), 23 September 2026
grade_reason: The only statement found since January 2025 calls for consumer protections and protection of critical infrastructure and refers to AI's risks only in general terms. Nothing found acknowledges catastrophic risk, and nothing dismisses it.
